content.title: WEIRD SIGNS YOU'RE ACTUALLY LOW ON A {{NUTRIENT}}
facts: **Vitamin A** – Struggling to see in dim light or at night, plus dry, gritty-feeling eyes.
**Zinc** – Food tastes bland, cuts heal slowly, and you're catching every cold going around.
**Magnesium** – Eyelid twitches, restless legs at night, and muscles that cramp out of nowhere.
**Vitamin B12** – Tingling or numbness in your fingers and toes, plus a pale or yellowish tint to your skin.
**Folate** – Constant fatigue, a sore smooth-looking tongue, and brain fog that won't lift.
**Iodine** – A puffy neck, feeling cold all the time, and unexplained weight gain.
**Vitamin E** – Muscle weakness, poor balance, and nerve pain in your legs.
**Omega-3** – Rough, sandpaper-like patches of skin and dry, brittle hair that won't grow.

caption:
A few of these are sneakier than people think. Low **zinc** doesn't just mess with immunity — it actually dulls your taste buds because zinc is needed to regenerate the taste receptor cells on your tongue, so food can start tasting weirdly flat. **Magnesium** shortage shows up in twitchy eyelids and restless legs because magnesium controls how your muscles and nerves relax after they contract — without enough, they stay slightly "switched on." And with **vitamin B12**, that tingling in your hands and feet happens because B12 is essential for maintaining the protective coating around your nerves, so a long-term deficiency can literally affect nerve signaling. Everyone's body is different, so listen to yours and get levels checked before assuming.
